summary: AstroSafe is a desktop application, written in Python, that lets a mission team monitor the health of astronauts from data stored in an SQLite database. In its current state it delivers two working screens: the crew overview and the individual crew member view. The remaining screens were designed but not built. Space agencies treat radiation exposure, microgravity effects and physiological stress as the main health hazards of spaceflight, and they track them with wearable dosimeters and regular medical measurements (Canadian Space Agency, n.d.-a, n.d.-b, 2026; National Aeronautics and Space Administration [NASA], n.d.-a, n.d.-c). Both agencies also run research programs on these hazards (Canadian Space Agency, n.d.-c; NASA, n.d.-b). AstroSafe applies that idea at student-project scale: a smartwatch reading arrives every second, and the app shows each astronaut's oxygen saturation, heart rate, body temperature, radiation dose, body composition and sleep in one place.
details: AstroSafe is a Python-based desktop application that enables mission teams to monitor astronaut health in real time using data stored in an SQLite database, simulating second-by-second smartwatch readings to track vital metrics such as oxygen saturation, heart rate, body temperature, radiation dose, body composition, and sleep quality. Its primary benefit lies in centralizing the three major spaceflight health hazards identified by agencies like NASA and the CSA—radiation exposure, microgravity effects, and physiological stress—into a single, intuitive interface featuring functional crew overview and individual member screens. The project's intended impact is to provide a scalable, student-level telemetry and preventative medical monitoring tool that mirrors real aerospace protocols. Developed with Python and SQLite, the project stands out creatively by translating complex aerospace medicine challenges into an accessible software architecture, with the team carefully considering real-time data flow efficiency, user interface clarity, and alignment with authentic space agency standards.
